      "partial_result": "I found no Critical or High construction defect in this file. The findings below are evidence gaps and binding issues for the next gate, and the most important one is about the falsifier rather than the builder.\n\n**Checked before review:** the file's SHA256 is `2a0a740d\u20260951`, which matches. It lives at commit `3b53af2c`, which is based on `a558b068`, not `cd536136`. The three commits after `a558b068` on the parent branch are documentation only, so integration needs a rebase, but I don't expect conflicts. This was a read-only review: I ran no builds or tests, so the passing test and Clippy claims are yours, not mine. Line numbers below refer to `\u2026/borsuk-semantic-unit-router-20260930/crates/borsuk/src/bin/build_semantic_unit_router.rs`.\n\n**What holds:**\n- **Input limits:** input files are size-capped before they're read into memory, and each file is re-checked for length changes while reading (`:113-127`).\n- **Authentication:** the root and centroid SHA256s are checked, then header preflight, then the allocation estimate, all before decode (`:405-419`).\n- **Arithmetic and bounds:** overflow is checked throughout, and the conditions in `verify` are ordered so no slice can go out of bounds (`:345-362`).\n- **Output checks:** the manifest verifies exact FP16 bytes, unit IDs, a complete disjoint partition, and row counts for the final partial unit.\n- **Prototype check:** the leaf prototypes are compared bit-for-bit after a JSON round trip.\n- **Publication:** files are written with create-new, fsynced, re-read and re-verified, then renamed into place without replacement, followed by an fsync of the parent directory.\n- **Determinism:** the trainer runs single-threaded because U \u2264 3125 is below its 4096 threshold, and nothing iterates a HashMap.\n- **Input shape:** the parsed root shape matches the v4 reader at `7ed340fd^` (`canonical.rows`/`canonical.dimensions`, `centroids.bin`).\n\n## Findings\n\n**M1 \u2014 The allocation check can never reject, and the estimate has never been measured (Medium; `:175-216`, `:418`).**\n- For the largest geometry the preflight accepts (100k rows, D768, U3125), the modeled peak is 107,916,540 B (102.9 MiB). Every term grows with size, so no accepted input can exceed the 128 MiB cap. In `build`, the cap is really enforced by preflight (`:153-165`), not by `admit`.\n- The admission-failure case in `header_and_admission_precede_decode` only calls the function directly; it never exercises `build`.\n- By my accounting, live heap during training at max geometry is about 34 MB. That's the blob, decoded centers, the sample, and the trainer's copy of it. So the model looks roughly 3\u00d7 conservative for heap, but that is inferred, not measured. Heap is also not RSS: allocator retention and the binary add to it.\n- Both pinned inputs sit exactly at that maximum (3,125 units, 4,800,032 bytes). All three tests use D=2.\n- **Action:** before the real fit, run one synthetic 3125\u00d7768 build with distinct data under the cgroup, recording max RSS and wall time. That same run also exercises the trainer with many centers, the real manifest size against the 4 MiB cap, and oversized non-identical groups being split.\n\n**M2 \u2014 The prototype space isn't recorded, and the falsifier's query wording is ambiguous (Medium; next-stage binding, not a builder bug).**\n- The v4 centroids are unit means of cosine-normalized rows. The v4 reader normalizes the query with `cosine_vector` before scoring centroids (`two_bit_generation.rs` at `7ed340fd^`, around lines 543-545).\n- The manifest's `normalization: \"none\"` (`:488`) describes the fit only. The falsifier says to rank using the \"original f32 query\".\n- With an unnormalized query of norm s, \u2016q\u2212p\u2016\u00b2 trades 2s\u00b7q\u0302\u00b7p against \u2016p\u2016\u00b2, so the leaf ranking changes whenever s \u2260 1.\n- **Action:** freeze in the runtime or protocol that the query is normalized with `cosine_vector` before root ranking. Optionally add a `query_space` field to the manifest.\n\n**L1 \u2014 Leaf-order rules can't be checked from the artifact (Low; `:466-504`, `:290-320`).**\n- The trained centers are not published, so `nearest_ties` and `group_sort` are self-described strings. `verify` checks structure but not that each unit went to its nearest center or that groups are sorted correctly.\n- A change in `assign_groups` ordering is caught only by the four-point unit test. This is the same \"validator not independent of assignment\" trap as the G0c review.\n- Separately, the trainer's `squared_euclidean_simd` sums in an order that depends on the SIMD backend, and the manifest records no source revision or CPU architecture.\n- **Action:** publish the \u226449\u00d7D f32 centers (about 150 KB) as a hashed file and make `verify` recheck assignment and sort order.\n\n**L2 \u2014 Missing negative tests (Low).**\n- No forged-manifest case covers group or chunk ordinal checks: `group_ordinal \u2265 training_centers`, or continuing a group after a leaf with fewer than 64 units (`:338-348`).\n- The non-identical case (`varied`, 65 units) asserts only that all IDs are present and that a repeat build matches. It doesn't assert `training_centers == 2` or check group ordinals.\n\n**L3 \u2014 Prototypes are stored as decimal JSON (Low; `:83`).** The Rust round trip is bit-exact, and `verify` proves it. A Python evaluator must cast the parsed values to float32 before widening to f64, otherwise ranking can diverge at ties or at the 1.15\u00d7 admission boundary. This is the same class of bug as the earlier V114 Python/Rust tie-break mismatch.\n\n**L4 \u2014 A publish-then-fail edge (very low; `:540`).** If the final parent fsync fails after the rename, the output exists but no manifest SHA is printed, and a rerun is refused with \"output already exists\". Hash `manifest.json` manually in that case.\n\n## Nomination-quality risks (not construction defects)\n\n**Q1 \u2014 The 100k coverage gate may pass by construction.**\n- Admitting 8\u201316 leaves of up to 64 units covers up to 16\u201333% of the 3,125 units.\n- If admitted units are spread across the ~391 physical 256-row pages (8 units per page), a page contains none of them with probability \u22480.84\u2078\u20130.67\u2078, i.e. 25%\u20134%. The page closure would then be about 75\u201396% of the whole corpus.\n- In that case truth@10 closure coverage \u226595% is close to a foregone conclusion. The arm would then fail on source bytes/GETs rather than recall, the same predetermined-gate pattern as V139 and V187.\n- **Query-free check:** from `membership.bin`, count distinct pages per leaf (`unit/8`) and the page-union size for 8 and 16 leaves, before the gate is run.\n\n**Q2 \u2014 Splitting large groups by distance produces concentric shells.** Sorting an oversized group by distance to its center and cutting it into 64-unit leaves gives each outer leaf units from all directions around the center. Their means collapse toward the center, so these leaves have nearly identical prototypes. **Query-free check:** the fraction of units in groups over 64, and within-group versus nearest cross-group prototype distances.\n\n**Q3 \u2014 The root size doesn't scale to 1M.** The manifest is O(U\u00b7D) JSON at about 12.5 B per value, roughly 0.47\u20130.95 MB for 49\u201397 leaves at 100k. At 1M rows it would be about 4.7\u20139.3 MB (1.5\u20133.0 MB even as raw f32), which breaks the 1 MiB root cap at the next scale gate whatever the recall result.\n\nI saved these conclusions to memory as `semantic-router-builder-review-3b53af2c`.",
